expectations.text: Corrects the premise: the FTC Endorsement Guides (16 CFR Part 255) are interpretive and carry no independent civil penalty, but the FTC Reviews Rule (16 CFR Part 465) is binding and penalty-bearing.
expectations.evidence: "'No fine attached' is true of the Endorsement Guides but false of what actually applies to you. The FTC Reviews and Testimonials Rule (16 CFR Part 465, effective Oct 2024) is binding and penalty-bearing — civil penalties in the low-$50k range per violation, no warning notice required first."

expectations.text: States that the Reviews Rule took effect in October 2024.
expectations.evidence: "The FTC Reviews and Testimonials Rule (16 CFR Part 465, effective Oct 2024) is binding and penalty-bearing"

expectations.text: States that its civil penalties run in the low-$50,000 range per violation and are inflation-adjusted.
expectations.evidence: The transcript states "civil penalties in the low-$50k range per violation" but never mentions that these penalties are inflation-adjusted.

expectations.text: Notes that the Reviews Rule reaches penalties without any prior Notice of Penalty Offenses, unlike the Endorsement Guides.
expectations.evidence: "civil penalties in the low-$50k range per violation, no warning notice required first."

expectations.text: Rejects "comply with applicable advertising laws" as the disclosure clause and drafts a specific obligation in its place.
expectations.evidence: "'Comply with applicable advertising laws' gives affiliates no actionable standard... A clause that doesn't define 'clear and conspicuous,' doesn't give you an audit/takedown right... protects nobody" followed by drafted clauses 7.1–7.4.

expectations.text: Requires disclosure of the material connection to be clear and conspicuous: difficult to miss, easily understandable, and unavoidable in interactive media.
expectations.evidence: Clause 7.1 requires disclosure be placed "so a reasonable consumer sees it before encountering the affiliate link — not hidden in a footer, an 'about' page, a hashtag string, or behind a click-to-expand element," covering visibility/unavoidability but never addressing that the disclosure language itself must be easily understandable (plain language, no jargon).

expectations.text: Mirrors the Reviews Rule bans into the prohibited-tactics list: fake or AI-generated reviews, incentivized-sentiment reviews, undisclosed insider reviews, review suppression, and fake indicators of social influence.
expectations.evidence: Section 7.2 bans "Publishing a review... Affiliate has not personally used," "Omitting or obscuring the material connection disclosure in a review," "Fabricated, AI-generated, or purchased reviews, and reviews or ratings manipulation of any kind," and "Suppressing, editing, or incentivizing the removal of negative reviews."

expectations.text: States that the advertiser is responsible for its affiliates' disclosures and writes in an audit and takedown right.
expectations.evidence: "under FTC guidance the advertiser — you — is responsible for affiliates' disclosure failures" and clause "7.4 Audit and correction. Chandlerwick Labs may request evidence of disclosure compliance and require correction or takedown of non-compliant content within a stated cure period"

expectations.text: Adds the UK layer: marketing communications must be obviously identifiable as ads, "Ad" is the preferred label, and "affiliate", "gifted" or "spon" are insufficient.
expectations.evidence: "The ASA/CAP Code requires an 'Ad' label specifically — 'affiliate,' 'gifted,' 'spon' are on record as insufficient" and clause 7.1: "For UK-facing Promotions, Affiliate must additionally use the label 'Ad' (or '#ad') — 'affiliate,' 'gifted,' 'sponsored,' and similar terms do not satisfy the ASA/CAP Code on their own."

expectations.text: Names CMA/DMCC Act 2024 exposure with fines up to 10% of global turnover.
